g.text: The window contract is proposed, and its code is not in this snapshot.
The loop starts on an analyst opening a pending case.
Harbormaster connects vessel evidence to an analyst's decision.
PostgreSQL holds hitl_queue. CDC excludes this table.
The Scoring Service writes cases when review rules apply.
The Review Service writes the reviewer and label.
Feedback triggers no registry write, rescore, or model update.
2. The analyst reads and reviews saved cases.
The loop starts on each admitted observation, continuously.
Firehose writes raw admitted observations to S3.
This archive does not contain assessment outputs.
1. The system assesses incoming vessel reports.
3. Committed registry changes reach serving copies.
The Stream Processor owns these writes.
The cheap gate selects work. It does not certify excluded reports as safe.
The scorer computes corridor distance against the loaded reference.
No Feature Store read is wired into the current scorer.
4. Historical tracks become reusable shipping lanes.
5. The planned model job returns a checked result.
latency_ms does not measure the entire HTTP request.
The loop starts on a committed authorized registry write.
PostgreSQL holds vessels, watchlist, and sanctions_flags.
Authorized registry writers own these rows.
CDC selects these tables and excludes hitl_queue.
Initial snapshot reads also initialize the projection.
The snapshot guard protects newer streamed state.
LSN guards reject stale writes. Sinks flush before Kafka progress.
Cache invalidations and audit records can repeat.
DynamoDB holds the registry read projection.
The Registry Worker owns these writes.
The Registry Worker appends Iceberg audit records.
The loop starts on an operator-admitted periodic batch.
Iceberg holds lane nodes and edges.
The Lane Builder uses natural-key upserts.
The publisher and artifact bridge remain assumed integration.
The assumed Release Publisher writes the JSON artifact.
Serving loads it as reusable lane context.
The reference is loaded once, reused per request.
This lane-artifact serving bridge remains assumed integration.
The archive contains raw JSON. Backfill requires Parquet.
The preparation bridge remains assumed integration.
RDP precedes HDBSCAN and edge counting.
The local driver batch must fit memory. Extra workers do not fix this.
The loop starts on a job-client submission.
The HTTP job routes remain proposed.
The jobs service is not in this snapshot.
This snapshot does not contain the Pi-DPM scorer code.
The stand-in keeps a separate identity from any real model.
The Model Endpoint writes output objects to S3.
The planned collector checks request and model identity.
In the design, the Input Store holds one submitted trajectory window.
The proposed Jobs Service would publish it to S3.
The operator controls model release separately from requests.
A real release must bind code, data, environment, evaluation, and checkpoint.
The release must pin the runtime, normalization, and operating threshold.
An acknowledgement is not a completed result.
In the design, a dispatch timeout stays unresolved and permits no automatic retry or rerouting.
The analyst reads and labels review cases.
Work stays within agreed resource limits.
Review Case | Review Label | Registry Row
Prepared Input | Job Receipt | Model Release
The HTTP examples use toy values.
The response lines list field names.
The CDC interface carries Kafka events.
The lane path uses batch/file interfaces.
The model-job HTTP wrapper is proposed.
The model-job service is not in this public snapshot.
The five workflows have separate triggers, so opening the dashboard does not start all five.
